drafted_from: tool:google-account-restore_mail_thread's own row in tools/read-and-write-gmail/tool-rows.json (invoke method, url, body_template, input and output schema); Gmail response values worked out from that row for the synthetic input
start_here: Say to your AI: "Restore conversation 18c1a2b3d4e5f601 from Trash. Use my Google account connection service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery." It runs tool:google-account-restore_mail_thread as that account and hands back the Gmail answer.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it calls Gmail for one Google account the connection names and answers what Gmail returns.
instructions: 1. Connect a Google account in your Workshop connections and note its handle, like service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery.

2. Say to your AI: "Restore conversation 18c1a2b3d4e5f601 from Trash." and let it call run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:google-account-restore_mail_thread, and the input {"connection":{"connection_id":"service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery"},"thread_id":"18c1a2b3d4e5f601"}.
3. Read what comes back: the request goes as POST  the Gmail me-mailbox base (gmail.googleapis.com, v1)/threads/18c1a2b3d4e5f601/untrash with no body.
4. Read the thread afterwards to confirm its labels.
